verses.1: Nebukadnezar, king of Babylon, served under the rule of Diahab Rumah. He was a true ruler who ruled over the land of Babylon.
verses.2: And Nebuchadnezzar, the king, sent messengers to Michnas, to Ahash-darfnyaya, and to Pahvatha Adargzraya. He also sent messages to all the rulers of his kingdom, so that they would come and worship before Nebuchadnezzar, the king.
verses.3: Bediyin are preparing for the arrival of Ahshdarpnaya, Sigenaya, and Pahvata Adargazraya. All rulers of the kingdom are going to be gathered here to receive the king who will be established as a ruler.
verses.4: And Khorozah called out in chorus, “Ammaiya Umayya!” and “Lishanaya.”
verses.5: In the time of those who heard the words of the prophets, there was a great noise and chaos. All kinds of songs and music were sung in praise of the image that was created by Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.6: And it will not fall or be destroyed at that time. It will remain hidden until the day comes when it will be revealed to those who are worthy.
verses.7: Everyone who receives this message at this time will hear it. All the people of Ammaya will be happy, and all kinds of songs will be sung. All the people of Ammaya will be blessed, and they will worship the image of Him who created everything.
verses.8: Everyone who receives the offering at that time should bring their offerings along with them. They will then eat those offerings, just as the Jews do.
verses.9: We replied and said to Nebuchadnezzar, “May your days be long and happy forever.”
verses.10: You have made a king who can make all people listen to his words. He is like a singer who sings beautiful songs. All kinds of music will be brought forth and used to praise his image.
verses.11: And Mayn-Di-La will not be destroyed; it will remain intact. It will become a source of joy for those who love it.
verses.12: May the Jews be blessed! They served the kingdom of Babylon, following its laws. But now, they have been freed from their servitude. Now, they can live in peace. There’s no need for them to follow those laws anymore. The ways you established are no longer valid.
verses.13: Bedarin Nevukadnazar Birgaz and Hamah said to Hayaia, “Go and save me from this situation.” And Bedarin Gubraya said, “I will go first.”
verses.14: Nebukadnezar replied to them, “The way is far from here. I will serve the Lord. I will not follow their ways. Nor will I follow their rules or their traditions.”
verses.15: Now, they will be gathered together in one place. They will hear the voices of those who sing hymns and praises to the Lord. All kinds of songs will be sung in praise of Him. They will not worship those who are not worthy of worshiping. But at that time, they will be brought before the Lord, who will judge them according to their actions.
verses.16: We have served Shadar from Mishaach, and we have also served Nego. We say to the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, do not be cruel; we are willing to submit to your rule.”
verses.17: May God, who is my Lord and my Savior, help me to avoid being deceived by those who are false and deceitful. May He also protect me from those who try to deceive me.
verses.18: And they do not know that the king who rules over you does not act in accordance with your wishes. The laws and regulations you established have not been followed at all.
verses.19: Bedayin Nevukadnazar became humble and submissive. He obeyed my commands completely. He served Nego, and he said to him, “For you, seven times over the course of time.”
verses.20: And the soldiers of Givreh, who were in the camp, said to him, “Please lead us away from here and serve Nego for our sake. May you be blessed.”
verses.21: Bedain Gubraya, let me go with them to their homes, to their fields and gardens. Let them be free from oppression and suffering.
verses.22: Everyone who receives blessings from the king’s words will be blessed. Let them go forth and serve Nego Katil Himmon Shiviba Dini Nura.
verses.23: And Gubraya, go and follow their path from there. They served Nego, but they fell into Goh-Atun-Nura. Yakidta was defeated by them.
verses.24: Adin Nevuchadnazar, the king, stood up in fear. He said to his people, “Now there are three groups of people who are suffering and in need of help. We must seek help from the king.”
verses.25: He replied, “I saw four men walking along the path. They were wearing armor and carried weapons. Their number was about four.”
verses.26: Bedeian Krerin Nevuchadnazar l’Ttra’ Athun Nur’a Yakidta’a. Anah and Amar Shadrk Mishach, and serve Nego, my servant, for the sake of Elaha. Puku eto Bedeian Napkin Shadrk Mishach, and serve Nego from Goh Nur’a.
verses.27: And they prepare Ahshadrafnyay, Pahvata, and the words of the king. I will go there, but not to a place where there is no light. Their doors are not open, and they refuse to let me in. The smell of oil doesn’t come from them at all.
verses.28: Nebukadnezar replied, “May the Lord bless you! You serve Nebuchadnezar, the king. May he grant you success in your work. May those who serve him be blessed by him. May they not fall into sin, nor worship any other gods instead of him.”
verses.29: And from me comes the taste of all nations of gods. And my tongue says, “May they be destroyed by those who rule over them.” They will serve Nego, the demon-possessed one. In his house, all who receive it will be destroyed. There is no other god besides Him; He alone can save us from destruction.
verses.30: Bediyin Malcha was able to escape from his captors and serve Nego in the kingdom of Babylon.
verses.31: May the king’s blessings be upon all nations and tribes throughout the world, so that peace may reign everywhere.
verses.32: May they and all those who serve me be blessed by the Holy God, before I go to Hawa.
verses.33: Oh, how vast and magnificent is His kingdom! How vast and powerful is His rule over it, day after day.
